title: Add callsite-aware token lifespan metrics and oncall alert orchestrator
author: Marisol Chen
release_notes: Adds a new callsite-aware token lifespan metric family, a compact Callsite Lifespan heatmap panel in the Console, and an oncall alert orchestrator that reduces noisy token-cost alerts by correlating per-callsite token lifespan regressions with recent deploys or kernel contention. No breaking API changes.
description:
Motivation: We see bursts of cost/latency noise originating from a small set of callsites (client callsites / SDK callsite tags) but existing token-cost and latency rollups lack the notion of where in the product surface the invocation originated. This PR introduces a callsite-aware token lifespan metric and a lightweight oncall alert orchestrator that correlates short-term increases in median token lifespan and tail with deploy windows, kernel queueing metrics, and model-variant fallbacks.

What this PR does: 1) introduces per-callsite token_lifespan histogram and derived median/p95 metrics (callsite.name, model, route, tenant); 2) implements a low-cardinality callsite normalization step that maps fine-grained callsite IDs to stable feature surfaces to avoid cardinality blowups; 3) exposes a new Callsite Lifespan heatmap panel in the Console showing callsites vs token-lifespan buckets with selectable time windows and attribution links to traces; 4) adds an oncall alert orchestrator that groups alerts by callsite impact, suppresses redundant token-cost alerts for the same callsite within a configured window, and attaches contextual evidence (recent deploys, kernel contention spikes, KV-cache miss rate) to the alert payload; 5) sampling and retention adjustments to keep metric volume bounded (reservoir sampling on rare callsites).

Implementation notes: All metric names are under redwood.observability.token_lifespan.*. The callsite normalization is implemented in telemetry/callsite_normalizer.go and uses a two-stage hashing+stable-name mapping with a TTL for automatic compaction. The heatmap is a new Console dashboard JSON with an adapter to link selected heatmap cells to the trace UI. The alert orchestrator lives in observability/alert_orchestrator and runs as an async worker that consumes alert candidates from the Alert Engine, enriches them, and issues grouped notifications.

Backwards compatibility: Existing token-cost and latency metrics remain unchanged. We add new metrics and a dashboard; users can opt-out of callsite normalization via a tenant config flag.

Testing and rollout: Unit tests added for normalization and sampling (telemetry/callsite_normalizer_test.go). Integration tests for the orchestrator simulate deploy events and kernel contention tags. Feature gated behind FF_OBS_CALLSITE_LIFESPAN. We will roll the dashboard as a soft-launch (Console feature flag) and progressively enable alert orchestration for internal tenants before customer-facing rollout.

CI notes: initial CI run surfaced a flaky integration test related to annotation ordering which was fixed in the second commit. The full CI matrix is green on merge.

Related work: builds on ENG-1421 (token attribution primitives) and OBS-78 (alert grouping RFC).

feat(console): add Callsite Lifespan heatmap panel and trace linking
feat(alerts): implement oncall alert orchestrator and grouping logic
chore(telemetry): add callsite normalizer and reservoir sampler
test: add unit and integration tests for normalizer and orchestrator
docs: runbook for oncall orchestrator and dashboard guide
review_comments: Amit Rao: Nicely scoped. A couple of suggestions: 1) ensure the normalization TTL default is documented and safe for high churn tenants; 2) can we expose a debug endpoint to list current normalized mappings for internal debugging?
Marisol Chen (author): Added TTL config and debug endpoint in the third commit. Updated docs with recommended defaults (30m TTL, 1000 unique callsites per tenant before compacting).
Sofia Kline: Alert grouping logic looks good. Please ensure we include a backoff variant when kernel contention metadata is low-fidelity (i.e. don't over-group on weak signals).
Marisol Chen: Adjusted grouping thresholds and added a fallback path that requires at least two corroborating signals (deploy, queueing, cache-miss) before suppressing separate alerts.
Jordan Park: Unit tests are thorough. Integration test flake reproduced locally; I recommend adding a small deterministic seed for the sampler.
Marisol Chen: Added deterministic seeding to integration tests and included a note in the test helper.
SRE Lead (approval): Approved. Recommend soft-launch to staging and internal tenants first.
ci_checks: integration-tests: pass (after rerun; original flake fixed)
